# Upgrade Duration SLOs

Whether platforms set P95/P99 upgrade time targets.

## Finding: No Platform Publishes Percentile-Based Upgrade Duration SLOs

After exhaustive search across Kubernetes, OpenShift, GKE, EKS, AKS, DOKS, IONOS, Rancher, and RKE2 documentation, **no platform publishes P95 or P99 upgrade duration targets** [20-28].

Platforms provide duration *estimates* and *formulas* but explicitly avoid SLOs. GKE publishes control plane uptime SLOs (99.5%-99.95%) but these do not cover upgrade duration [26].

## OpenShift: The Most Quantitative Approach

OpenShift provides a deterministic formula for upgrade duration [20]:

```
Cluster update time = CVO deployment time + (# node update iterations × MCO node update time)
```

| Component | Duration |
|---|---|
| CVO (pod-based updates) | 60-120 minutes |
| MCO (per node) | 5+ minutes |
| Cloud instance reboot | 1-2 minutes |
| Bare metal reboot | 15+ minutes |

**Example calculations (minimum values — MCO uses 5+ min floor)** [20]:
- 3 control plane + 6 compute nodes, maxUnavailable=1, cloud: 60 + (6 × 5) = **90 minutes (minimum)**
- Same cluster, maxUnavailable=2: 60 + (3 × 5) = **75 minutes (minimum)**

**Image Based Upgrade (IBU)** for telco use cases reduces upgrade time to approximately **15-20 minutes** [28].

## Universal 4-Hour Maintenance Window

AKS, GKE, DOKS, and IONOS all converge on **4 hours** as minimum/default maintenance window [23] [25], suggesting industry consensus despite no published SLOs.

## Counter-Perspectives: Why Duration SLOs Are Impractical

**Environmental variation (7-15x):** Bare metal reboots take 15+ minutes vs 1-2 minutes in cloud — a single variable that makes universal targets impractical [20] [27].

**PDB-induced unpredictability:** Restrictive PDBs can force GKE to wait up to 1 hour per node for graceful eviction [25]. Setting minAvailable=100% prevents voluntary disruption entirely.

**Speed vs safety tradeoff:** "Rushing upgrades leads to outages" — proper pre-upgrade validation (API checks, etcd backup, staging) adds time that cannot be compressed without risk (discovery agent, Tier 2-3).

**Engineering effort ≠ upgrade duration:** A single minor upgrade across 3 regions consumes 4-6 weeks of engineering effort [70], and 30+ clusters face 6-8 hours per cluster rebuild with full-week fleet rollouts [71].

**GKE batch limitation:** GKE upgrades ~20 nodes simultaneously regardless of maxSurge setting, meaning a 2,000-node pool requires ~100 batches minimum [25].

## Metric Taxonomy

| Metric | Type | Measurable By |
|---|---|---|
| CVO deployment time | Duration range (60-120 min) | Vendor-measured |
| MCO per-node time | Duration (5+ min) | Operator-measurable |
| Control plane upgrade | Duration (5-15 min cloud) | Operator-measurable |
| Maintenance window | Threshold (4 hours) | Operator-configured |
| Total cluster update | Calculated from formula | Operator-calculable |

## Gaps and Limitations

- No P95/P99 SLOs exist anywhere in the ecosystem
- OpenShift provides the only published formula; other platforms use vague language ("several minutes", "a few hours")
- Duration ranges (e.g., 60-120 min for CVO) are not specified as P50, P95, or observed max
- Real-world timing data comes primarily from Tier 3-4 sources (blogs, tutorials), not official benchmarks
- The 4-hour maintenance window convergence may reflect operational practice rather than engineered guarantees
